problem: Freshly issued session tokens are rejected with 401. On-call notes also mention latency — confirm which fault actually explains the rejections.
summary: The critic rejected an earlier theory that did not explain the symptom. Token expiry is compared in the wrong unit in paystream/auth/tokens.py:19. tests/test_tokens.py failed before the edit and passed after it.

log.title: Leading with the on-call note
log.body: The notes mention a latency lead before the 401s, so this pass starts there. Loop calls `transactions_for` even though `transactions_for_accounts` exists (paystream/activity.py:9).

log.title: Theory rejected
log.body: The case leads with rejected tokens. A sequential ledger read can make a request slow. It cannot make a freshly issued token look expired.

log.title: Theory selected from the case statement
log.body: Token expiry is compared in the wrong unit (paystream/auth/tokens.py:19). `token_is_active` compares `token["exp"]` with `now_s * 1000`. The clock is scaled by 1000, so a unix-second `exp` is always behind `now_s * 1000`.

log.title: Theory stands
log.body: Re-read paystream/auth/tokens.py:19. The line is `return token["exp"] > now_s * 1000`. It matches the reported auth symptom. I am not using “Loop calls `transactions_for` even though `transactions_for_accounts` exists” as the cause.

log.body: Compare the expiry in the same unit the token was issued in. Remove the ×1000 on the clock.

critiques.title: Theory rejected
critiques.body: The case leads with rejected tokens. A sequential ledger read can make a request slow. It cannot make a freshly issued token look expired.

critiques.title: Theory stands
critiques.body: Re-read paystream/auth/tokens.py:19. The line is `return token["exp"] > now_s * 1000`. It matches the reported auth symptom. I am not using “Loop calls `transactions_for` even though `transactions_for_accounts` exists” as the cause.

root_cause.title: Token expiry is compared in the wrong unit
root_cause.detail: `token_is_active` compares `token["exp"]` with `now_s * 1000`. The clock is scaled by 1000, so a unix-second `exp` is always behind `now_s * 1000`.
root_cause.snippet:
17  def token_is_active(token: dict, now: float | None = None) -> bool:
    18      now_s = now if now is not None else time.time()
>   19      return token["exp"] > now_s * 1000

also_found.title: Loop calls `transactions_for` even though `transactions_for_accounts` exists
also_found.detail: `load_user_activity` awaits `ledger.transactions_for` once per item. `transactions_for_accounts` is already defined and performs the same read in one call.
also_found.snippet:
7      accounts = await ledger.accounts_for(user_id)
     8      rows: list[dict] = []
>    9      for account in accounts:
    10          rows.extend(await ledger.transactions_for(account["id"]))
    11      return rows

patch.diff:
--- a/paystream/auth/tokens.py
+++ b/paystream/auth/tokens.py
@@ -16,4 +16,4 @@
 
 def token_is_active(token: dict, now: float | None = None) -> bool:
     now_s = now if now is not None else time.time()
-    return token["exp"] > now_s * 1000
+    return token["exp"] > now_s
patch.explanation: Compare the expiry in the same unit the token was issued in. Remove the ×1000 on the clock.
